title: Liar’s Poker
description: Bid on your hidden number, bluff, and call the computer’s bluffs. The two numbers are never compared.
versionOrder: Within each capture, save order is retained. Cross-capture ordering is a presentation guess; tape numbers do not establish development dates. Similarity clusters are provisional, and collected saves are not necessarily revisions of one program.

quickHelp: Click the screen. You and the computer each hold a secret number. A bid claims “my number is above this.” Type a bid, or CALL to challenge the computer’s bid. Only the last bidder’s number is checked: above the bid, the bidder wins; otherwise the caller wins. See “How to play” for the rules.

howToPlay.heading: The idea
items: Each hand, you and the computer each get a secret number from 1 to 10000. You see only yours.
A bid claims “my number is above this.” You may bluff. On screen, the current bid is called THE POT, and “raise” means bid. It starts at 0 each hand.
The two numbers are never compared with each other. You win by catching the other side bidding above its own number, or by being called when your number is above your bid.

howToPlay.heading: Your turn
items: At TYPE ‘CALL’ OR YOUR RAISE, type a higher number and press Enter to bid. Or type CALL, in capitals, to challenge the computer’s last bid.
Either side may go first, chosen at random each hand. The computer then bids (I RAISE IT TO …) or calls (I CALL).

howToPlay.heading: When someone calls
items: Only the last bidder’s number is revealed and checked against the bid.
Number above the bid: the bidder wins.
Number at or below the bid: the caller wins, so a tie goes to the caller.

howToPlay.heading: Example: you hold 3000, the computer holds 9000
items: You bid 2000 and the computer calls: you win, because 3000 is above 2000. The computer’s higher number does not matter.
You bid 9500 and the computer calls: you lose, because 3000 is below 9500.

howToPlay.heading: Score
items: You both start with 20. Each hand moves 1 point from the loser to the winner.
The game never ends by itself, and scores can go negative. Use Restart for a new game.

howToPlay.heading: How the computer plays
items: It always raises when its number is above the current bid.
Otherwise it bluffs with another raise if the bid is below a hidden limit it picks each hand, and calls if not.
Each raise adds a random amount, up to a maximum chosen once per game.

howToPlay.heading: Quirks in the 1970s code
items: A bid equal to the current one is accepted, even though the game asks for a raise.
If you call before any bid, you lose: the computer’s number is always above 0.
A bid above 10000 is accepted, but if the computer then raises, the program stops with an error.
